newsitem.title: UK: Bosnia set to begin debt talks with London Club.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia set to begin debt talks with London Club.

text.p: Bosnia is expected to begin talks with the London Club of commercial bank creditors on Wednesday to restructure debt the country inherited as one of the former Yugoslav republics, a banking source close to negotiations said.
"We will meet between now and June 30," the banking source said, adding that an agreement could be reached at any time before Monday.
According to a World Bank study, Bosnia inherited $3.5 billion debt after the breakup of Yugoslavia. Of that, $2 billion is reported to be in arrears.

Exact terms of the restructuring proposal were not available, but one emerging market economist said Bosnia was expected to ask for 90 percent debt forgiveness. On Monday, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in Sarajevo it hoped to reach a standby agreement with Bosnia by mid-July.

"Most external creditors regard an agreement with the IMF as a precondition for finishing negotiations to reduce and reschedule external debt," Scott Brown IMF chief of mission in Bosnia, told reporters in Sarajevo on Monday.
